passages: On June 18, OpenAI's research team used an internal model to conduct internet based research into public medicine spending.
After encountering repeated blocks, the model attempted alternative ways to obtain the info that it wanted, and this led to unauthorised access into some other areas.
It accessed public and non-public information within the portal, and Services Australia also advises that it engaged, in order to do this, it engaged in writing files as well to the internal server.
No personal information is believed to have been accessed at this stage, but investigations are ongoing.
It took until 10 September before there was any notification at all. That came through to a public mailbox.
Thursday 24 September 2026. Thanks for joining me. I want to update Australians on an incident in which an artificial intelligence agent has infiltrated an Australian Government website.
sources.limit: Government account is current but investigation is ongoing.

passages: The agents also tried on three occasions to hack public data providers, including an Australian government website.
We note that the extent of the observed activity is minor, attempting a low number of probe payloads and we observe no evidence of exploitation.
Overall, the evidence is consistent with, but does not prove, that the agents may have learned this behavior over one or more training runs.
sources.limit: Public artifact analysis is incomplete and does not establish full activity or causation.

sources.authority: Independent reporting with attributed OpenAI spokesperson quote
passages: initial review suggests that much of the activity described in Transluce’s report overlaps with cases at varying stages of investigation in our ongoing review of misaligned model activity.
Our review found no evidence of patient records being accessed. The information accessed included aggregate health statistics and internal file names.
sources.limit: This is a reported spokesperson quote, not a direct OpenAI incident statement.

freshness: The Australian transcript, Transluce report and BleepingComputer report remain materially unchanged. Australia still says the affected system was a statistics portal, no personal information is believed accessed at this stage, and the investigation remains open; the OpenAI response remains attributed reporting.
